verdict.rationale: DBOS's core value proposition is that it's an open-source, Postgres-backed library with no proprietary orchestration server — all workflow/checkpoint state lives in the user's own Postgres database, which is inherently open and exportable via standard SQL tooling (dbos-docs-2, dbos-docs-20, dbos-docs-23, dbos-comm-13). The CLI can list workflows in JSON (dbos-docs-41), and Conductor (the hosted management layer) can also be self-hosted (dbos-docs-19, dbos-docs-34), reducing lock-in risk. However, there is no explicit documented 'export all your data' feature/guide, no migration tooling, and community comments note some hosted pieces (observability) were not self-hostable at points in time (dbos-comm-8), so full data portability for the managed/Cloud tier isn't concretely evidenced. Missing for 10: explicit data-export documentation/tooling, confirmation that Conductor/Cloud-hosted metadata is fully exportable, and independent verification of a clean 'leave' path from the hosted service.
